label: early original-phase input of w/n/q/k/g/s/a (positions 1-5)
explanation: Candidate unit 0 high end. 93% of activation mass is in the original (input) phase, almost all at positions t=1-5 (peak t=2-3, 64% of mass). It never fires at t=0 and almost never at the delimiter or late original positions (t>=6); there is a weak secondary tail in the copy phase (6% of mass), mostly at recall_idx 2-6. Within the early window, activation depends graded on the current input token: w is strongest (25% rate, 21% of mass; all top examples are w at t=3-4), then n, q, k, g, s, a, with l/u/2/p weaker. It is further boosted by the sequence first token (h, 1, m, 0, f raise rate 2-3x), and favors first occurrences of the input token. These factors combine additively, so no clean boolean rule: the window+token predicate gets dev F1 ~0.46 (precision 0.37, recall 0.60, mass recall 0.69); the position window alone has mass recall 0.93 but precision 0.13.
